newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares cheered up by dollar and Dow.
newsitem.headline: German shares cheered up by dollar and Dow.

text.p: German shares perked up in post-bourse dealings on Thursday, boosted by a firmer dollar and strength on Wall Street, after a rather lacklustre performance in floor trade.
The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computerised dealings in the DAX index of 30 top German shares, jumped off earlier lows in the afternoon to end up 10.60 points, or 0.38 percent, at 2,824.83 points.
The market was encouraged as Bunds, the dollar and Wall Street rose after a larger-than-expected drop in the U.S. trade deficit in October to $7.99 billion.
Earlier the DAX index had ended listless bourse dealings down 13 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,807.75 points.
Dealers said the market now had the potential for a bit of Christmas cheer and said the DAX index could push up to 2,850 points on Friday.

News that the Bundesbank had left interest rates unchanged, as expected by most analysts, and that the M3 money supply growth target corridor for 1997 would be 3.5 to 6.5 percent both failed to inspire the share market.
Thursday was the last trading day for the December DAX futures contract and dealers said that had led to some volatility in the day's dealings as players moved to cover their futures positions.
The December DAX contract closed at 2,825 points.
Traders said the expiry of futures contracts on individual shares had also led to volatility in stocks such as industrial group Daimler, electronics group Siemens and insurer Allianz.

Meanwhile, shares in speciality chemicals group Henkel KGaA, powered ahead, gaining 2.4 percent or 1.74 marks to 74 marks, after its said it planned to acquire the remaining 23 percent of consumer products group Hans Schwarzkopf that it does not already own.
Henkel, best known for its Persil washing powder, took over a majority stake in Schwarzkopf last summer, which helped it boost its results considerably.
Shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen also staged a late afternoon rally, ending IBIS dealings up 9.25 marks at 628.75 marks.

Dealers said hopes for an out of court settlement in VW's legal battle with U.S. giant General Motors Corp. had crept back into the market, despite GM saying on Wednesday no talks with VW were planned.
